title: Split a joined pair of disposable chopsticks cleanly and lay the two sticks side by side across a lunch jar
instruction: Split the chopsticks and lay them ready across the lunch jar.
context: Disposable chopsticks come as one piece: two sticks joined at the head, which the eater snaps apart before the meal, or a server or carer does for someone who cannot. Pulled apart evenly near the tips they split cleanly down the slit; pulled carelessly they turn in the hands instead of opening, or split unevenly and leave one stick with a splintered head. Each stick is only about 5 mm thick with a 2 mm slit beside it, so each hand must hold one stick alone, and the two pulls must act at the same place along the pair: a pinch cannot stop a thin stick turning, so hands set even 3 cm apart along the pair spin it and then shear the two sticks past each other, an uneven split. The two grippers therefore work side by side, about 5 mm between fingertips. The split sticks are then laid back across the jar, tips together, ready to pick up. A pair is used once: every trial needs a new one (about 4 US cents).
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Place mat: IKEA SVARTSENAP place mat, grey woven cotton, 451 x 349 (17 3/4 x 13 3/4 in), about 2 thick (estimate), flat on the table, long side along y, centred at (262, 0). 2) Food jar: Thermos Stainless King 16 oz food jar, midnight blue body, stainless steel lid, closed and empty: 142 high, 94 wide, 363 g (maker's listing 5.6 in, 3.7 in, 0.8 lb); lid top flat, about 88 across (estimate). It stands on the mat, centred at (255, 0). 3) Chopsticks: one unsplit pair of bamboo twin disposable chopsticks, 240 long, pale natural bamboo, no sleeve (for example Yanagi Products P-422, pack of 100). Each stick about 4.8 x 4.8 in section, slit about 2 wide, the two joined over the last 35 at the head, about 3.9 g a stick (estimates). The pair lies flat across the middle of the lid, both sticks on it, long axis along x, centre line on y = 0, eating tips toward the robot at x = 135, head end at x = 375; its top is about 151 above the table and each end overhangs the lid by about 75. 4) Nothing else is on the table. Gripper pads bare. Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end from a photo, a ruler and the trial video. 0: the pair is still one piece (wherever it is), or a stick has left the table. Otherwise the pair is split in two. Clean split: each stick whole along its length, the widths of the two heads within 2 mm of each other (ruler), no splinter longer than 10 mm, nothing broken off. Laid ready: both sticks lie flat on the jar's lid, each overhanging the lid at both ends, eating tips at the same end with a gap of 10 mm or less between them, the two sticks within 10 degrees of parallel, both grippers at least 30 mm away from both sticks, nothing moving. 1.0: clean split and laid ready. 0.75: clean split, not laid ready (still held, apart, crossed, on the mat or the table). 0.5: uneven split, laid ready. 0.25: uneven split, not laid ready. In simulation the sticks cannot splinter: a split counts as uneven when, as the joint let go, the two tips moved further past each other (along the sticks or across their thickness) than apart across the slit.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. A split pair cannot be reused: take a new pair from the pack for every trial (about 4 US cents; a pack of 100 costs about 4 dollars). Set aside any pair that is cracked at the head, warped, or whose slit is closed. Once per pack, a one-minute check on a spare pair: hold one stick flat on a table edge, hook a kitchen scale (or a loop of string on it) round the other stick 15 mm from its tip and pull sideways until the pair splits; use the pack if the scale read 250 to 600 g (2.5 to 6 N). Stand the empty, closed jar on a tape mark on the mat, centred 255 mm in front of the midpoint between the arm bases. Lay the new pair flat across the middle of the lid, tips toward the robot 135 mm out, head away, along the centre line (a tape line on the lid helps). Before the first trial of a session, check that the two arms can hold their fingertips 5 mm apart: command both to the grip pose with no pair on the jar and look; if the fingertips touch or sit more than 2 mm off, recalibrate first. Wipe the lid. No food or liquid is used; the jar's cost is about 28 dollars, the mat's about 2.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Each stick is one rigid 3.9 g body; a fixed joint at the slit's root breaks for good at 0.8 N m (estimate: about 4 N at the tips), so the pair splits only when the sticks are really pulled apart. Sticks cannot bend, crack or splinter: an uneven split is a rule on how the tips parted. The two grippers work side by side, fingertips about 5 mm apart while holding: a real trial needs arm tracking of about 2 mm. Jar and mat are plain solids at the listed sizes.
